In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

pericentromere rearrangements, including isochromosomes, are a common feature of HNSCC, and that they may be associated with a poor prognosis, but the exact mechanisms of the formation of these rearrangements, and their clinical significance, still need to be elucidated.
the breakpoints of the pericentric rearrangements in HNSCC are not clustered in any particular region, and that the breakpoints may be anywhere in the pericentro-meric region of chromosome 4.
pericentromer rearrangements, in general, are not specific for HNSCC, and that they are not specific for chromosome 5.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pericentomeric rearrangements of chromosome 5, such as isocromosome formation, whole-arm translocation, and double-minute formation, are not the result of a single mechanism, but rather the consequence of different genomic rearrangements, which may occur independently in the same tumour cell.
the pericentric region of chromosome 6 is involved in structural rearrangements in a number of cases of head and neck squamocellular carcinomas (HSCC).
pericentromere rearrangements in HNSCC can be explained by the occurrence of a single event in the majority of cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to use FISH techniques to characterise the precise breakpoints of chromosome 5 rearrangement in order to understand their biological significance.
FISH analysis is a useful adjunct to the study of pericentric chromosome abnormalities.
